title: Three Years and One Short Bib
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：track　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 track 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the athlete ① followed the track that no trainer in the stadium would have counted, and he said the following was the whole of the year. The ② track, meaning the path itself and not the bib, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a track, he said, is the only thing in a stadium that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ track in that stadium had the same short bib beside it, and the ④ track at the far track, meaning the lap they kept for the children to count and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A track, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the athlete said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the track was the whole of the matter, meaning the progress and not the path. The ⑥ track, meaning the progress and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; track, he said, is either something you follow or the only word that means both a path and a progress. He said the progress is the part they remember.

By 1988 the ⑦ track had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short bib. The ⑧ track of the whole thing, the athlete wrote in September, was one stadium and three years of counting; track, he said, is either the lap at the far track or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ track I remember is the path counted in the programme, which closed in 1990 and is still counted as the quietest in the stadium. A ⑩ track, my mother said in 1992, is the only path that improves by being counted; every track, she said, is a progress that has agreed to look like a path. She said the progress was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 跑道；足迹（指体育场里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 跑道；足迹（指那条跑道本身，与小小的号码布相对）
C. 固定搭配：follow the track 循这一条跑道
D. n. 跑道；足迹（指留给孩子们数的那一圈）
E. n. 跑道之事（抽象总称，指一处体育场的跑道之事）
F. n. 跑道；足迹（指秩序册里写到、被清点的那一条）
G. n. 跑道、进展（指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 进展（抽象总称，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: followed the track that no trainer in the stadium would have counted

the track at the far track

answers.why: follow the track 意为“循这一条跑道”，1983 年那位运动员把体育场里没有一位陪练肯清点的一条跑道做了一遍。
track 意为“跑道；足迹”，指那条跑道本身而不是小小的号码布，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被清点。
track 意为“跑道；足迹”，指体育场里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一块小小的号码布。
track 意为“跑道；足迹”，指最远那条跑道的留给孩子们数的那一圈，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
track 意为“跑道、进展”，指一件事里人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条进展就是那件事的全部。
track 意为“进展”，指人人都跑却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条跑道，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
track 意为“跑道；足迹”，指秩序册里写到、被清点的那一条，到 1988 年这一条成了秩序册里的一行。
track 意为“跑道之事”，运动员九月写道，整件事的跑道之事是一处体育场和三个年份的清点。
track 意为“跑道；足迹”，我记得的是秩序册里清点过的那一条，1990 年跑完了，至今仍被说成体育场里最安静的一条。
track 为抽象总称，母亲 1992 年说，跑道是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的跑道。
